scope_and_objective: CI/CD pipeline evolution and restructuring in open-source software projects; identifies restructuring operations and analyzes how CI/CD pipelines evolve over time.
corpus_and_data_sources: 8,000 GitHub projects using CI/CD infrastructure; 615 manually analyzed pipeline-configuration-change commits.
method_and_outputs: Manual coding, card sorting, metric extraction. Outputs: a taxonomy of 34 CI/CD restructuring actions and 16 Travis-CI metrics/facts.
relation_to_present_slr: Relevant for understanding CI/CD pipeline evolution, maintainability, performance, and security. Does not focus on IoT, CPS, or DevOps practices across IoT architectural layers.

scope_and_objective: Adoption of microservices and DevOps in CPS, especially for modernizing legacy systems; investigates challenges, practices, and migration rationales.
corpus_and_data_sources: 146 scientific papers + 9 interviews with CPS professionals; sources include Google Scholar, ACM DL, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink.
method_and_outputs: Rapid review combined with an interview-based case study; thematic analysis and card sorting to identify CPS-specific challenges/practices.
relation_to_present_slr: Relevant because CPS and industrial IoT share constraints (hardware dependency, heterogeneity, real-time behavior, safety, distributed operation). Focuses on CPS modernization rather than DevOps, CI/CD, and DevSecOps integration across the IoT lifecycle.

scope_and_objective: Comprehensive review of IoT testing: testing types, methods, tools, challenges, validation strategies, sensor-specific concerns.
corpus_and_data_sources: IoT testing studies published from 2012 onward, complemented by an industrial IoT case study.
method_and_outputs: Taxonomy- and framework-oriented synthesis; outputs a sensor-aware taxonomy of IoT testing challenges and a multidimensional framework relating architectural layers, testing objectives, and technology targets.
relation_to_present_slr: Relevant for testing automation, CI/CD, DevOps, edge computing, security testing, interoperability, regression testing, hardware-in-the-loop validation, and digital twins. Testing-centered; does not provide a DevOps-centered lifecycle classification of frameworks and practices.

scope_and_objective: Survey of DevOps techniques applied to cloud-based IoT mashups; examines correlation between DevOps technical practices and tools that enable continuous integration, test automation, rapid deployment.
corpus_and_data_sources: 50 references drawn from the DevOps and IoT literature via a structured mapping approach; no formal multi-database query reported.
method_and_outputs: Structured thematic mapping; papers assigned to seven categories (methodologies, result reports, influence, fundamentals, challenges, knowledge, implementation); comparative survey of IoT cloud platforms in tabular form.
relation_to_present_slr: Relevant as an early survey of DevOps toolchains and orchestration mechanisms for cloud-based IoT. Lacks formal inclusion/exclusion criteria, does not address the full IoT architectural stack, and is not lifecycle-oriented or maturity-based.

scope_and_objective: Challenges of adopting DevOps culture in IoT applications; assessed along four effectiveness dimensions (collaboration, sharing, efficiency, quality); proposes the Industrial DevOps Maturity Model (IDMM) guideline framework.
corpus_and_data_sources: 35 primary studies from ACM DL, ScienceDirect, Web of Science, Google Scholar, Wiley, IEEE Xplore, supplemented by snowballing; Tollgate quality checklist and thematic categorization.
method_and_outputs: Systematic literature review; outputs a taxonomy of challenge categories and the five-stage IDMM (Initial, Managed, Defined, Qualitatively Managed, Optimized).
relation_to_present_slr: Relevant for the motivational/challenge-oriented dimension of DevOps adoption in IoT. Scope limited to organizational and cultural challenges; does not cover the technical practices, tools, or architectural layers addressed in the present SLR.

scope_and_objective: Empirical investigation of how IoT systems projects adapt to achieve continuous delivery, focusing on differences from traditional development, quality practices adopted, and cultural/technical/business challenges.
corpus_and_data_sources: 31 semi-structured interviews + a follow-up questionnaire with 30 additional professionals, from development/operations/hardware backgrounds in Brazil, Germany, the Netherlands, and Portugal.
method_and_outputs: Qualitative empirical study inspired by grounded theory; open coding into categories; interview transcripts. Outputs: 15 practices ranked by adoption frequency and conceptual challenge maps across cultural, technical, and business dimensions.
relation_to_present_slr: Relevant as practitioner-grounded evidence of continuous-delivery challenges in IoT projects, particularly CI/CD automation, IaC adoption, and hardware/firmware integration. An empirical/interview study rather than a literature review; does not classify practices/tools by IoT architectural layer or DevOps lifecycle stage.

scope_and_objective: DevOps in IoT software systems; investigates DevOps concepts, benefits, challenges, tools, and programming languages/pipeline stages for IoT.
corpus_and_data_sources: 26 primary studies retrieved from IEEE Xplore Digital Library, ACM Digital Library, ScienceDirect, Springer, Wiley.
method_and_outputs: Qualitative analysis based on open coding. Outputs include categories of benefits/challenges, tools, programming languages, and a perceived DevOps pipeline for IoT.
relation_to_present_slr: Closest prior work to the present SLR because it explicitly studies DevOps in IoT systems; its synthesis is mainly descriptive and does not provide a detailed lifecycle-oriented classification or maturity analysis across modeling, deployment, orchestration, monitoring, testing, security, privacy, and risk assessment.

scope_and_objective: DevOps, CI/CD, CICD, and DevSecOps integration in IoT systems across the cloud-edge computing continuum; explains why DevOps is strategic for IoT and identifies frameworks supporting its integration.
corpus_and_data_sources: 172 studies retrieved from WoS, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and Scopus (NOTE: manuscript Table V header cell states 172; this conflicts with the 219/xx/122 figures elsewhere in the same draft -- see ../../docs/known-issues-and-todos.md). Search strategy includes DevOps-related terms and IoT-related synonyms derived from reference standards.
method_and_outputs: Lifecycle-oriented synthesis; classifies frameworks according to IoT engineering needs and maps them to research areas and architectural layers.
relation_to_present_slr: Provides a broader and more structured synthesis than previous work. Identifies architectural layers, research areas, framework categories, and open challenges for DevOps, CI/CD, and DevSecOps adoption in IoT systems.
